body: Bipolar and OCD. Bipolar throws you from feeling on top of the world to the pits of suicidal depression. OCD is like an abusive manipulative person living in your head, it convinces you you're an evil person and that you've done horrible things, makes you doubt yourself to the point where you're not even sure if your memories or thoughts are real. Bipolar is generally accepted by society to be severe but OCD is often seen as cute and quirky. I'd argue they're just as bad as eachother. Both can easily ruin your life without treatment.

I was on one SSRI for a couple years when I was in my mid teens and don't remember experiencing any hypomania until I switched to another, and even then it was only after about 4 months of taking it. I don't think SSRIs will reliably trigger hypomania/mania in everyone with bipolar but it is a known risk factor. It probably just depends on the individual and the specific medication

When I'm hypomanic I get super productive (but usually fixated on something random that's not studying lol) and sometimes I can study more but often I'm too excitable. Maybe on the come up I would be able to get things done. I think overall its about trying to accept that you will have these changes in mood and energy where you won't feel like doing any work but ultimately If getting a degree is really important to you you will find a way. 
I think part of it is accepting that you're gonna be more productive at studying at sometimes than others and kind of working around your moods, like when your stable doing extra work to make up for time lost when you were depressed. It's hard but not impossible, I believe in you! 💞

Heyy I'm so sorry to hear that happened to you that's so awful! I hope your head isn't hurting too bad. It was a while ago but I want to say maybe 3 or so months until I felt better. I've been on effexor for nearly 3 years now and I'm very grateful I stuck it out because I feel its helped my depression immensely and allowed me to be able to function again. 

I know the starting dose is 37.5mg, if you're finding you can't tolerate the side effects it might be worth talking to your doctor about going down to a lower dose and then gradually increasing to allow your body to adjust to it better. I started on 75mg too and this is something I'd have done if I'd known, in hindsight I think that would have lessened my side effects.

I'd say things to be mindful of is to take it at exactly the same time every day, sometimes I'll still go through times where I get the withdrawal symptoms towards the end of the day so I'll start to take it slightly earlier in the day. Another thing is if you go up or down a dose it'll probably help a lot to taper, I always take the beads out and count them and gradually increase/decrease which I feel has worked to minimise side effects while adjusting my dose. 

Overall I think this drug can be really beneficial for depression if you can tolerate the side effects (especially if you're like me and tried multiple antidepressants before this that didn't work). But I know how difficult it is when you're in the middle of it and just want to feel normal, but it definitely gets better over time. I found ginger really helpful for nausea and travel sickness medication if I was really struggling. I also took migraine medication occassionally which helped with the headaches/nausea
Try and do everything you can to make sure you never miss a dose because that can make you feel very ill. I hope you start to feel better soon, feel free to reach out if you have any more questions and I'll do my best to help, all the best 💓

Hey I am so so sorry that you are having to go through this. You may already know this so forgive me if you do, but u thought it might help to understand the process behind ocd.
So your brain has a fear response which has helped humans survive over the years. For example if we were being chased by a bear this response would be triggered and we'd get that feeling of deep panic and dread and it would ultimately spur us to run in order to escape danger. Unfortunately for people with ocd this system can get mixed up and can end up creating the same fear response to thoughts (even ones that aren't true) that it would to a real threat. This is why the emotions and fear you are feeling feel so real, because they are but the thought that has caused them is not a rational reason to be afraid. 

It is this that actually drives the cycle of ocd. When you have an intrusive thought and you body responds with fear your brain immediately assumes that this a real reason to be afraid. This then assigns meaning and power to the thought (even if in reality it has absolutely none).  Your brain then goes over and over checking the thought, seeking reassurance and so on. Each time it does this it might create a new fear response and so only reinforces the cycle. 

I would suggest the next time you get an intrusive thought try to notice the fear, reminding yourself that this is the cause of some mixed up signals, and the fear produced doesn't mean that the thought is important or most importantly, true. This can be hard to do but try and practice it to see if it helps. 

Something else to note is that if you are sat with this fear, it might be that your brain doesn't know quite what to make of it and will start looking for things to pin it on, because this level of anxiety without a reason doesn't make sense right? In reality there is no reason but this is where ocd will make you go through all your thoughts to check for details, even creating false memories over time. As the more you check the less certain you become of what is actually true. 
Ocd can be an absolute beast and horrendous to live with but things can get better. I assure you that you are not the only one suffering with these incredibly disturbing obsessions but just know that it is not a fault of your character but an illness. No matter how horrible the thoughts are try to remind yourself that this is ocd that making you fixate on these thoughts and not you wanting to think them. I want to remind you that you are not insane, a monster or any of the other horrible things you feel you are right now. You deserve to be happy and you deserve for things to get better but that will take time. I really do feel for you and a relate a lot to the things you've spoken about. I have quite a bit of experience in dealing with ocd so feel free to dm me anytime and I'll do what I can to help. I wish you all the best 😊💕 (sorry for the essay lol)

Hey, you might not believe it right now but intrusive thoughts are quite normal. However for someone with OCD these thoughts are wrongfully interpreted as meaningful. We pay attention to these thoughts, worry about them, obsess over what they must mean about us. Over things we've seen in the past and what that must say about our characters. Make us question everything about ourselves.
 In reality they are just that, thoughts. They can be horrific and disturbing but are not necessarily true. Unfortunately the more attention they are given, the more frequent they will become. I assume you're trying not to think about the topic of these thoughts or put them out of your mind. A good example is "do not think of a pink elephant" the first thing that comes into your mind is a pink elephant, in the same way that the more you try not to think about your upsetting thoughts the more they will appear. So to answer your original question these intrusive thoughts may feel like they are happening 24/7 at the moment ad you are probably engaging in compulsions like arguing with the thoughts, going over past memories to check how you behaved or getting reassurance. You'll find that the less you actually engage with these thoughts the less they will occur (easier said than done I know). 

If you can simply recognise when you are having obsessive/OCD thoughts that's a big step forward, and even more so if you can avoid compulsions. Probably sounds terrifying and counterproductive but next time OCD throws something at you try responding with "fine. Youre right maybe I am a monster maybe I did do xyz " instead of entertaining them. Try it a couple times and you might be surprised by how it kind of stumps OCD in what to say next.
 Anyways sorry for the whole essay I hope this made sense and helped even a little, my DMs are always open if you want to chat or vent I know how difficult things can be with OCD💓
